question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I raised an order with a backup supplier for the Lacrivia/Cyclosporine plant (PL-01), but no approved backup covers the Oculon path. Oculon has enough stock today, so I made no allocations. At the current shipping rate, Oculon will likely drop below safety stock at every warehouse (DC) in about 2–3 weeks and could run out in about 4–5 weeks. I escalated that to the Supply Planning lead. This run is flagged for human review: the process doesn't cover a backup supplier that serves only some of the plants, and no playbook matched, even in discovery mode.

**What I found**
- **Late shipment:** the next S-103 shipment is PO000210, 3,300 units of RM-103 (glycerin), promised 2026-10-03. With a 4-week slip it ships around 2026-10-31. The three later S-103 orders (PO000211–213) may slip too.
- **Products affected** (trace_supply_exposure, current BOM edges):
  - At plant PL-01: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine OS (FG-1003).
  - Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001/2002): RM-103 goes into an ingredient made by contract manufacturers S-202/S-203, which plant PL-02 uses.
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 is qualified for RM-103 and active, but approved to ship only to PL-01. So it covers Lacrivia and Cyclosporine OS, not Oculon. The process's decision point assumes the backup covers every plant or none, so it doesn't fit this case.
- **Stock against safety stock (2026-09-25 snapshot):**

| Product | DC | On hand | Safety stock | Days of supply |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oculon 2.5 mL | Central | 293 | 120 | 35 |
| Oculon 2.5 mL | East | 417 | 180 | 33 |
| Oculon 2.5 mL | West | 268 | 100 | 39 |
| Oculon 5 mL | Central | 109 | 46 | 32 |
| Oculon 5 mL | East | 177 | 70 | 35 |
| Oculon 5 mL | West | 77 | 38 | 27 |
| Lacrivia 5 mL | East | 46 | 471 | – |
| Lacrivia 10 mL | East | 34 | 233 | – |

  - The Lacrivia shortfall at the East DC already existed before this delay.
- **Recovery:** about 46 days from the material arriving until finished product reaches the DCs, including the 14-day sterility test. Oculon from the delayed shipment reaches the DCs around mid-December 2026.
- **Substitutes:** Oculon has no approved company substitute. Lacrivia's approved substitute, Cyclosporine OS, uses the same material, so it can't be offered. Medical Affairs guides alternatives.

**Actions taken**
1. **Purchase requisition PR-D4825649:** S-111, 3,300 units of RM-103, ship to PL-01, needed by 2026-10-10 (original ship date plus 7 days' transit).
2. **No allocation and no approval request.** Oculon is at or above safety stock at every DC. Lacrivia is covered by the backup order, so the rules (BR-ALLOC-02) exclude it.
3. **Case CASE-CFAA4135 (Supply Planning lead):** asks them to:
   - get S-103 to rush or split-ship the RM-103 for the Oculon path;
   - assess an emergency approval of S-111 for PL-02 and the contract manufacturer sites;
   - re-run the allocation step for Oculon once any DC drops below safety stock.

   It also notes the existing Lacrivia shortfall at the East DC and the process gap.
4. **CRM tasks for the five contracted health systems' account teams.** Each says: no allocation for now, the expected recovery date, and the substitute position.

| Account | Tier | DC | CRM task |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northfield (AC00117) | A | East | CRM-9162B578 |
| Oak Hollow (AC00038) | A | East | CRM-9463A949 |
| Riverbend (AC00059) | A | West | CRM-7D9945E5 |
| Clearview (AC00001) | B | East | CRM-79BEE2B8 |
| Sunridge (AC00138) | B | East | CRM-2598CD02 |

5. **Case CASE-061AAE69 (Trade Relations):** notify wholesalers W-01 to W-06 across all three DCs. The wholesaler messaging system has no API, so I handed this to Trade Relations instead of sending it myself.

**What I didn't do, and why**
- **No order to S-111 for the Oculon path:** S-111 isn't approved for PL-02 or the contract manufacturers. Qualifying it is for Quality and Procurement (in the case).
- **No allocation and no approval request:** nothing met the allocation trigger, and I can't move stock between DCs without Supply Planning approval.
- **Wholesaler stock not checked:** that inventory feed isn't live until Q4 2026.

**Assumptions**
- "Next shipment" means PO000210. The order quantity copies that PO because I couldn't tell how much of it was meant for each plant; Procurement may need to cut it to PL-01's share.
- Recovery dates use standard manufacturing times and the supplier's 4-week estimate. The run-out estimates use the last 28 days of shipments and ignore Oculon already in production.
- The trade-customer notices went only to the five health systems with supply contracts.

**Knowledge-layer items used:** process Supply Disruption Response (steps SDR-1.1 to SDR-4.2), rules BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-REGION-01, BR-CUST-01 and BR-APPR-01, policy POL-DUA-01 (no patient-level data used), and reference sets supply_contracts, approved_substitutes and dc_service_regions. No playbook applied (none found, including in discovery mode).

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103' AND (STATUS='OPEN' OR SUPPLIER_ID='S-103') ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT DESC
SELECT SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, QUALIFIED_FLG, PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT PLANT_ID, MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','CMP-320','SEMI-060','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, PLANT_ID

SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, m.MATERIAL_TYP, m.MATERIAL_DESC FROM dbo.BOM b JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID WHERE b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','CMP-320') OR b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','SEMI-060')

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG, s.TIER, s.SUPPLIER_NM FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','RM-103') OR sm.SUPPLIER_ID IN ('S-103','S-111')
SELECT PLANT_ID, MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'CMP-32%' OR MATERIAL_ID LIKE 'RM-10%'

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND i.SNAPSHOT_DT = (SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV) ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID, SUM(s.UNITS) AS units_28d, SUM(s.UNITS)/28.0 AS avg_daily, MIN(s.SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(s.SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,(SELECT MAX(SHIP_DT) FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP)) GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY s.MATERIAL_ID, s.DC_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
acct AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, p.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) AS TOP_ID FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p ON a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=p.ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON p.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=gp.ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT t.ACCOUNT_ID, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.STATE, r.PROD_NDC11, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx13
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr ON pr.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN acct ON acct.ACCOUNT_ID=pr.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=acct.TOP_ID
WHERE t.ACCOUNT_ID IN ('AC00117','AC00038','AC00059','AC00001','AC00138') AND r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110','99101020205','99101030325','99101030350')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,4

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM, SUM(s.UNITS) units_90d FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s JOIN dbo.WHSLR w ON w.WHSLR_ID=s.WHSLR_ID WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-2001','FG-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND s.SHIP_DT > '2026-07-01' GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM ORDER BY s.DC_ID, units_90d DESC

escalation_cases.subject: RM-103 / S-103 4-week delay: Oculon (PL-02 / CMP-320 path) has no approved alternate supplier – projected safety-stock breach before recovery
escalation_cases.details:
Disruption: S-103 (Castellan Excipients) will ship its next RM-103 (Glycerin USP) shipment, PO000210 (3,300, promised 2026-10-03), about 4 weeks late (~2026-10-31). The later open S-103 POs (PO000211 promised 10-10, PO000212 10-18, PO000213 10-25) may also slip; please confirm with the supplier.
Mitigation done: PR-D4825649 raised with S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) for 3,300 RM-103 to PL-01. That covers Lacrivia FG-1001/FG-1002 and Cyclosporine OS FG-1003 (SEMI-044/045 at PL-01). S-111 also has an open PO000228 (5,300, promised 2026-10-17).
GAP: S-111 is approved only for PL-01 in the supplier portal. RM-103 also feeds Oculon FG-2001 (99101-0303-25) and FG-2002 (99101-0303-50) through CMP-320 (made by CDMOs S-202/S-203) -> SEMI-060 at PL-02. There is no approved alternate for that path, and Oculon has no approved company substitute.
Oculon DC position (snapshot 2026-09-25; on hand / safety stock / days of supply over the last 28 days): FG-2001 CENTRAL 293/120/35d, EAST 417/180/33d, WEST 268/100/39d. FG-2002 CENTRAL 109/46/32d, EAST 177/70/35d, WEST 77/38/27d. All are at or above safety stock today, so no allocation was made under BR-ALLOC-02.
Recovery: the delayed RM-103 arrives ~2026-10-31 plus 46 days of lead time (get_lead_times, BR-LEAD-01, incl. 14-day sterility release). Oculon made from it reaches the DCs around mid-December 2026. At the current run-rate, the DCs will drop below safety stock in about 2–3 weeks and run out in about 4–5 weeks, unless supply already in the pipeline covers the gap.
Asks: (1) expedite or split-ship with S-103 for the RM-103 that feeds CMP-320/PL-02; (2) Quality/Procurement to assess emergency approval of S-111 for PL-02 / the CMP-320 CDMO sites; (3) re-run SDR-3.1 allocation for Oculon as soon as any DC falls below safety stock.
Also noted: Lacrivia FG-1001 (46 vs SS 471) and FG-1002 (34 vs SS 233) were already below safety stock at DC-EAST. No allocation was made because the packs are covered by the qualified alternate (BR-ALLOC-02). Under BR-SUB-01/02 there is no company substitute at DC-EAST: Cyclosporine OS is fed by RM-103 too. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.
Process note: the alternate covers only part of the network (one of two plant paths), which SDR-2.1's decision conditions do not address. No playbook matched, even in discovery. Please review this run.
